shortDescription: Manage upload, installation, and removal of UCS files

options.name: force
options.description: If C(true), the system uploads the file every time and replaces the file on the device. If C(false), the file is only uploaded if it does not already exist. Generally should only be C(true) in cases where you believe the image was corrupted during upload.

options.name: include_chassis_level_config
options.description: During restoration of the UCS file, includes chassis level configuration that is shared among boot volume sets. For example, the cluster default configuration.

options.name: no_license
options.description: Performs a full restore of the UCS file and all the files it contains, with the exception of the license file. The option must be used to restore a UCS on RMA (Returned Materials Authorization) devices.

options.name: no_platform_check
options.description: Bypasses the platform check and allows installation of a UCS that was created using a different platform. By default (without this option), installation of a UCS created from a different platform is not allowed.

options.name: passphrase
options.description: Specifies the passphrase that is necessary to load the specified UCS file.

options.name: provider
options.description: A dict object containing connection details.

options.name: reset_trust
options.description: When specified, the device and trust domain certs and keys are not loaded from the UCS. Instead, a new set is generated.

options.name: state
options.description: When C(installed), ensures the UCS is uploaded and installed on the system. When C(present), ensures the UCS is uploaded. When C(absent), the UCS is removed from the system. When C(installed), the uploading of the UCS is idempotent, however the installation of that configuration is not idempotent.

options.name: ucs
options.description: The path to the UCS file to install. The parameter must be provided if the C(state) is either C(installed) or C(activated). When C(state) is C(absent), the full path for this parameter is ignored and only the filename is used to select a UCS for removal. Therefore you could specify C(/foo/bar/test.ucs) and this module would only look for C(test.ucs).
